description: Hi! I'm interested in space, technology, business, and product innovation. I enjoy researching problems and turning ideas into practical solutions. I have experience in business research, product management, UX/UI design, and prototyping with Figma and AI tools. I'm working on VOSTOK - Humanity's Next Mission, a lunar outpost simulation. I love exchanging ideas and collaborating with people from different backgrounds.
summary:
VOSTOK is an interactive pixel-art game designed to help children aged 7–12 learn about life on the Moon. It was developed for NASA’s “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” challenge.

In the game, players become astronauts and manage a lunar outpost over five simulated days. They make decisions about choosing a landing site, managing power and water, protecting the crew, growing food and communicating with Earth. Each decision affects the next mission, helping players understand how different systems work together.

VOSTOK turns space science into a fun, hands-on learning experience. It encourages children to think, solve problems and understand the challenges astronauts may face while living on the Moon. Our goal is to make space exploration more exciting and accessible to the next generation.
details:
VOSTOK is a browser-based lunar survival game where children aged 7–12 experience what it might be like to live and work on the Moon.

The game follows a five-day mission in which players take on the role of an astronaut responsible for establishing and maintaining a lunar outpost.

Each day introduces a different challenge:

  • Day 1 – A Home on the Moon: Choose a landing site and begin setting up the outpost.
  • Day 2 – The Sun Sends a Warning: Respond to a solar-event warning and make decisions to protect the crew and essential systems.
  • Day 3 – The Missing Water Mystery: Investigate a water-system problem, repair it and manage limited water supplies.
  • Day 4 – Can We Grow Food on the Moon?: Explore a greenhouse experiment and balance the needs of plants, water and power.
  • Day 5 – Mission Control Can't Answer Right Away: Investigate a communication problem and prepare the outpost for the future.

Players manage important resources such as power, life support, crew safety and water. Their decisions affect the resources and conditions carried into the next mission. This helps children understand that keeping a lunar habitat running requires different systems to work together.

The goal of VOSTOK is to make space science more engaging and accessible. It encourages curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving and responsible decision-making.

What makes the project creative is its combination of a pixel-art adventure game with simplified lunar mission challenges. Instead of only reading about space exploration, children learn by exploring, making choices and seeing their consequences.

Tools and Development: VOSTOK was developed as a browser-based game using Google AI Studio. AI-assisted coding was used during development, along with iterative testing and improvements to the gameplay, interface and visual experience.

AI Use Acknowledgement: Google AI Studio and AI-assisted tools were used to support code generation and development. The project was developed as an educational simulation inspired by space research; its gameplay and resource systems are simplified and are not a validated model of an actual lunar mission.
